summary: Unexpected duplicate tool executions after client-side multiplexed retry window with partial acks
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart reports that when using the Go SDK with multiplexed streaming sessions they observe duplicate external tool executions (webhook posts) in a narrow race where the client triggers a retry during the server-side retry window. Impact:
- Duplicate downstream side effects (payment webhook charged twice) in ~0.8% of long-running sessions for one major flow.
- Billing discrepancies and customer-facing incorrect behavior.
Environment:
- SDK: redwood-go v0.12.3 (custom wrapper)
- Service: Hosted Redwood Dedicated pool (us-east-1)
- Model: redwood-13b-v1 pinned to v2026-02-26
- Traffic pattern: multiplexed client with two concurrent logical streams per connection, median request time 18s, tail 90s
Observed behavior:
1) Client sends request A invoking external tool (payment POST) and receives partial ack for call queued but connection is swapped (connection migration) at ~17s.
2) Client times out locally, then triggers an immediate retry on the multiplexed session.
3) Server retries the in-flight tool call (because it had queued it) AND the client retry causes the tool to be enqueued again for the retried request resulting in two webhook posts.
Expected behavior:
- Server-side deduplication or explicit tool-confirmation should prevent duplicate external tool invocation in this race.
Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start redwood-go client with multiplexing enabled and two logical streams per TCP connection.
2) Use a handler that triggers a synchronous external webhook call during model generation.
3) Simulate transient connection swap (tcp reset) at ~15-20s on in-flight stream A.
4) Immediately retry the request on the same multiplexed session.
5) Observe two webhook calls for a single logical action.
Logs/trace snippets (redacted):
- correlation-id: bc-prod-9f3d
- server request id: srv-20260312-5031
- webhook upstream: https://payments.brightcart.com/charge -> 2x POST bodies with identical payloads timestamped 18.042s and 18.129s
- client side: "stream: moved, retrying request" followed by "retry-sent: idempotency-token=blank"

Temporary workaround requested by customer: guidance on short-term mitigations (headers, retry backoff, SDK flags).
steps_to_reproduce: See description steps; customer provided a minimal repro that toggles multiplex=true and forces a connection swap. They used an internal script to send SIGPIPE to the socket after 15s.
logs: server-log-excerpt: [2026-03-12T15:14:10Z] srv-20260312-5031 streamA queued tool POST -> outbound webhook payment id X123; [2026-03-12T15:14:27Z] connection migration detected; [2026-03-12T15:14:27Z] client retried logical streamA -> queued tool POST -> outbound webhook payment id X123 (second)
comments: 2026-03-12 - BrightCart-Support: We saw two charges for order 98765. Both webhook bodies identical. This wasn't reproducible on non-multiplexed config.
2026-03-12 - Support (Ava Patel): Thanks for the report — tagging Runtime and SDK teams. Can you share connection reset sequence and SDK version? Any idempotency token being sent?

2026-03-12 - BrightCart-Support: Using redwood-go v0.12.3, our wrapper strips idempotency headers for tool calls to reduce payload size (we didn't realize they'd be needed). We attached server logs. Repro is included.

2026-03-12 - Support (Luis Moreno): Reproduced locally with repro. Observed same double-enqueue when client retries immediately after reset and idempotency header absent. Raising to Runtime eng for dedup policy review.

2026-03-13 - Runtime Eng (Maya Chen): Observed that queued tool entries persist across connection handoff; dedupe map keyed by per-request ephemeral nonce was blank when client retried. Proposing server-side strong dedupe on (session-id, tool-hash) for a short TTL.

2026-03-13 - SDK Eng (Rajiv Kapoor): SDK change candidate: ensure SDK includes idempotency-token header for each tool request by default and preserve it across retries. Preparing PR for default behavior and docs update.

2026-03-13 - Support (Luis Moreno): Sent interim guidance to customer: enable `disable_multiplex=false` or add client-side deliberate 200ms jitter before immediate retry; both reduce duplicates pending fix.
investigation_notes: Runtime logs show queued-tool entries survive connection swap because queue is per-worker, not per-connection.
Deduplication currently relies on client-supplied idempotency token; if missing, server treats each enqueue as unique.
Multiplexed sessions allow retries to reuse logical stream identifiers; client immediate retries currently do not re-use/forward original token in this customer's wrapper.
Hypothesis: two independent code paths enqueued the same payload: the original in-flight path and the retry path after client reconnect. Without token, server cannot collapse them.
Repro steps run in staging reproduces at ~0.7% of requests when artificial swap injected; higher with aggressive client retry logic.
Potential edge case: cleanup TTL for queued-tool dedupe map configured to 30s; race window may be shorter than cleanup frequency.
resolution: Workaround provided to customer on 2026-03-13: a) enable per-tool idempotency tokens in their wrapper; b) add 150-300ms backoff before immediate retry; c) disable multiplexing as a short-term mitigation.

Engineering action items: (1) SDK: default to attaching idempotency-token header for tool calls and preserve it across retries (PR prepared by Rajiv K). (2) Runtime: implement server-side short-term dedupe by (session-id || request-hash) with a 60s TTL to collapse duplicate enqueues when token absent (proposal by Maya C). (3) Docs: add best-practice guidance for long-running tool calls under multiplexing with examples for Go/TS/Python (tracked in GH issue).
Planned rollout: SDK change staged in next minor release (v0.12.4) after review; runtime dedupe gated behind config flag for dedicated pools and will be rolled out to us-east-1 in canary first.
Follow-up: After SDK patch deployed, ask BrightCart to re-run repro and confirm no duplicates. If duplicates persist, collect full traces and reopen.
